chunks: He is the Living. There is no god but He. Therefore pray to Him with obedience all-exclusive. Praise be to God, the Lord of all the worlds.

key_terms.الْحَيُّ: The Ever-Living, one of the divine attributes
key_terms.لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ: There is no god but He (declaration of monotheism)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'mukhliseen lahu ad-din' in supplication?
ai.summary: This verse, known as the 'Verse of the Forgiver' (Ayat al-Ghaffar), is central to Shia supplicatory traditions, particularly in the Du'a al-Faraj, where it serves as a bridge between divine uniqueness (Tawhid) and the hope for intercession. It underscores the necessity of sincerity (ikhlas) in worship, a core tenet in Shia theology, while affirming God's absolute sovereignty over all creation.
